run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T02:35:37Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is firing because frontend's calls into product-catalog fail. Frontend error-status span rate went from 0 (samples up to 02:34) to 24.3 spans/s at 02:44, and the errors sit on exactly the routes that depend on product-catalog (GET /api/products/{productId}, /api/recommendations, /api/checkout) while /api/cart and /api/data show zero errors. The cause is a rollout of Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog at 02:33:46 that set the container command to "invalid-command": the new ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf replaced the previously healthy pod, every container start fails with exit code 128 / reason StartError "exec: \"invalid-command\": executable file not found in $PATH", the pod is in CrashLoopBackOff with 5 restarts and Ready=False, and the product-catalog Service has no ready endpoints. Callers recommendation, checkout and frontend-proxy show their own error spans on the same product-catalog dependencies. flagd fault flags are all off, so fault injection is not the cause. Who or what applied the deployment edit could not be determined because change history is not integrated.

claims.text: At 2026-11-18T02:44:00Z frontend carried an error-status span rate of 24.33 spans/s (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) alongside 18.22 spans/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET, i.e. the alerting signal is real in span telemetry for service frontend.

Frontend error spans were zero at every 2-minute sample from 02:20 through 02:34 and first became non-zero at the 02:36 sample (GET 5.4 spans/s, POST 0.55 spans/s), so the deviation began between roughly 02:34 and 02:36 — after the product-catalog rollout at 02:33:46, and before the alert start of 02:35:37 it had already begun.

Frontend errors are confined to product-catalog-dependent paths at 02:44: GET /api/products/{productId} 6.07 spans/s, executing api route /api/products/[productId] 6.07, GET /api/recommendations 1.23, GET /api/checkout-related POST /api/checkout 0.75, and frontend client spans grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 6.07, grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations 1.23, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.75; GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and GET /api/data were 0 over the same series.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog (generation 4) has spec.template.spec.containers[0].command = ["invalid-command"] for image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, and its status shows Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable since 2026-11-18T02:34:03Z, updatedReplicas 1, readyReplicas absent.

The rollout is visible as two ReplicaSets owned by Deployment product-catalog: old product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 02:03:45, command null, replicas 0) and new product-catalog-fcf7564cf (created 02:33:46, command ["invalid-command"], replicas 1); both use the identical image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, so the change was a configuration (command) change, not an image change.

Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l is Running but Ready=False (ContainersNotReady) with restartCount 5 and state CrashLoopBackOff ("back-off 2m40s restarting failed container=product-catalog"); its last terminated container has exitCode 128, reason StartError, message "failed to create containerd task: ... exec: \"invalid-command\": executable file not found in $PATH", and its container limits are cpu 15m / memory 30Mi.

Pod events for product-catalog record the same start error and the rollout: Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-2fvnx Failed at 02:33:51 with "exec: \"invalid-command\": executable file not found in $PATH", Deployment scaled down product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc 1->0 at 02:33:55 with the old pod killed, Deployment scaled up product-catalog-fcf7564cf 0->1, new pod vjj7l Scheduled 02:34:03 and Failed again at 02:37:16 with BackOff count 25.

product-catalog server-side span rate was healthy before the rollout (7.5 at 02:18, 13.0-13.4 spans/s at 02:24-02:36 samples) and collapsed afterwards (0.34 at 02:42, 0 at 02:44 and 02:45), and its server spans currently carry rate 0 with no error status series.

Service product-catalog (clusterIP 100.64.32.100, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog) has only notReadyAddresses (pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l, ip 100.96.2.148) and no ready address, so requests to it cannot reach a serving backend.

Other callers show their own error spans on product-catalog dependencies: recommendation 1.86 error spans/s (client span /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts 0.93 and internal get_product_list 0.93), checkout 1.18 error spans/s (client span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 0.59 and server span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.59), and frontend-proxy 12.24 error spans/s (ingress 6.13 and router frontend egress 6.11).

Background error level is small and pre-existing: ad held 0.0037 error spans/s at 02:30 (before the deviation) and 0.0043 at 02:45, frontend-proxy held 0.004-0.011 error spans/s at 02:20-02:30 before jumping to 2.68 at 02:35 and 14.13 at 02:40, and checkout/recommendation at those services' dependent operations only appear after 02:35.

Frontend itself was not changed and is running: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 since 02:03:46, ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 (created 02:03:46, command null), and non-product-catalog routes /api/cart and /api/data show zero error spans — the frontend failures follow from a dependency, not from a frontend-side change.

flagd fault injection is not the cause: ConfigMap flagd-config key demo.flagd.json lists every fault flag (including productCatalogFailure, paymentFailure, cartFailure, adFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) with defaultVariant "off", so no product-catalog fault flag was switched on.

OOMKill / memory pressure is not the mechanism: the product-catalog container's last termination reason is StartError with exit code 128 (exec: "invalid-command" not found), not OOMKilled, and the reported memory limit is 30Mi.

Checked and found without observed errors: cart carries 13.50 spans/s of STATUS_CODE_UNSET traffic with no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series returned, and currency/email/shipping/quote returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series (currency STATUS_CODE_OK 0, email/shipping/quote STATUS_CODE_UNSET 0); accounting, fraud-detection and payment returned explicit 0 error rate.

Restore product-catalog by removing the invalid command override from Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog (return the container to the image's default entrypoint, as the old ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc had) and rolling it out, then confirm the pod reaches Ready, the Service gets a ready endpoint, and frontend/recommendation/checkout error rates return to baseline.

gaps: Change history is not integrated in this Run, so who or what applied the command ["invalid-command"] to Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog (and exactly when the spec was edited) could not be observed; the rollout itself is dated by events and ReplicaSet creation at 02:33:46.

Application logs could not be used as evidence: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 returned zero lines (status no_data, no previous instance) and for product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l zero lines (container never started, no previous instance).

Jaeger returned no traces for service frontend or product-catalog in 02:20-02:45Z (services are listed but no traces matched), so span status tags / error descriptions for the failing calls are unverified; the error signal rests on traces_span_metrics_calls_total.

Prometheus returned no series for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready or kube_deployment_status_replicas_available with namespace=otel-demo, deployment=product-catalog, so deployment readiness is only known from the Kubernetes object, not from a metric series.

The old healthy product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-wzpwm was deleted at 02:33:55, so its logs and image_id digest cannot be read; the command difference is established from the two ReplicaSet specs and the same image tag, not from image digests.
